avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive anticoagulant/antiplatelet effects; increased bleeding risk with bevacizumab-induced thrombotic complications
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E to <400 IU daily or avoid; monitor for bleeding signs

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (concentrated extracts)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Platelet aggregation inhibition compounds bleeding risk associated with bevacizumab therapy
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue high-dose garlic supplements; discuss with oncology team before use

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Antiplatelet effects potentiate bleeding risk; may interfere with wound healing
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid during bevacizumab treatment; inform prescriber of any prior use

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce immune responses that could interfere with monoclonal antibody efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use with close clinical monitoring and dose adjustment consideration

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (fish oil)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet properties; generally well-tolerated but additive bleeding risk possible
caution_supplements.action: Use standard doses (<3g/day); monitor for excessive bleeding; document use

caution_supplements.name: Curcumin/Turmeric
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet effects and potential wound healing impacts
caution_supplements.action: Limit to culinary amounts; avoid high-dose supplements without oncologist approval

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: Generally safe; ensure quality/sterility given immunosuppressive effects of therapy
caution_supplements.action: Use well-established, quality-controlled probiotic strains; monitor GI tolerance

avoid_foods.name: Excessive alcohol (>2 drinks/day)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases GI bleeding risk, impairs wound healing, and potentiates hepatotoxicity; bevacizumab already elevates GI perforation risk
avoid_foods.action: Limit to ≤1 drink/day or abstain; counsel patient on bleeding complications

caution_foods.name: High-sodium processed foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Bevacizumab increases hypertension risk; excess sodium exacerbates this effect
caution_foods.action: Encourage DASH diet; monitor blood pressure regularly; limit sodium to <2.3g/day

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit/grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: Theoretical concern for immune modulation; not direct interaction but caution with immunotherapy
caution_foods.action: Occasional consumption acceptable; avoid excessive daily intake

caution_foods.name: Raw/undercooked foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Bevacizumab can compromise immune function; increased infection risk with foodborne pathogens
caution_foods.action: Practice food safety; ensure proper cooking temperatures; avoid high-risk foods (sushi, unpasteurized dairy)

monitoring_notes: Bevacizumab is a protein therapeutic not metabolized by CYP enzymes, reducing traditional drug-drug interactions; however, bleeding risk is paramount—monitor for hemorrhage, GI perforation, and delayed wound healing. Regular blood pressure monitoring is essential as hypertension is a common adverse effect requiring dietary sodium restriction and concurrent antihypertensive management.
